newsitem.title: CANADA: NBA BASKETBALL-BIG COUNTRY REEVES GETS SIX-YEAR EXTENSION WITH GRIZZLIES.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BIG COUNTRY REEVES GETS SIX-YEAR EXTENSION WITH GRIZZLIES.

text.p: Canada will be home to Big Country Bryant Reeves the next seven years.
The Vancouver Grizzlies announced the signing of the hulking centre to a six-year contract extension Tuesday at undisclosed financial terms.
Reeves was part of a Vancouver team that was an NBA-worst 14-68 last season, but is undergoing an overhaul.
Brian Hill took over as head coach on June 26, a day after the Grizzlies made highly regarded point guard Antonio Daniels the fourth overall selection in the draft.

The sixth overall pick in the 1995 draft, Reeves enjoyed a solid season in 1996-97, averaging 16.2 points and 8.1 rebounds in 75 games. The seven-footer (2.13 m) averaged 13.3 points and 7.4 rebounds during his rookie campaign.
On the front line with him is Shareef Abdur-Rahim, who was in the running for this season's Rookie of the Year award, and another 1996-97 rookie, Roy Rogers.

"The announcement today sends a message, I believe, to our fans that we continue to be committed to building a championship team here," said Grizzlies general manager Stu Jackson. "We don't want to lose the cornerstones of our franchise.
"'Big Country,' obviously, is a big, big key to our future success."
